name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,234

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drive to the end of old dock finally, after heading away from uncertain places

definitions.text: Drive to the end of old

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and sending it away removes that letter
finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: limbos are states or places of uncertainty
last letter of dock

explanation.surface: A driver heads off from vague places to reach the far end of an old dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of old' marks the sense as obsolete: this is an old hunting word. 'Drive' looks like motoring, but it means hounding a quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: In old hunting language, to imbosk or emboss a quarry was to chase it until it was exhausted, pushing it to its extremity.

clue.text: Junk associated with raid at sea, current danger to swimmers

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A Chinese junk on a raid at sea, with dangerous currents threatening anyone swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' and 'at sea' suggest a ship, but junk is just letters here. The Irukandji is a tiny, highly venomous Australian jellyfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irukandji jellyfish of northern Australian waters has a sting that can kill bathers, a real hazard on beaches.

clue.text: Credit outspoken school making a stand

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so we want the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: to credit a story is to buy it, believe it
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: Praise for a forthright school that takes a principled stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a stand' sounds like protest, but a stand is a support. Credit means believe, i.e. buy, which is heard as BI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipod is a two-legged support, such as the rest for a rifle or a camera, so it is a type of stand.

clue.text: Mean to swallow duck, like a shark

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: squalid means mean, sordid
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A shark is mean enough to swallow a duck whole.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Mean' an adjective about the shark's nature; it is the source of the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaloid is the zoological adjective for sharks and dogfishes, from Latin squalus, a kind of sea fish.

clue.text: United again finished with Gunners in place aforementioned

blocks.note: U is short for United in team names
bis is Latin for twice, an encore call meaning again
time is up when it is finished
the Royal Artillery are the gunners

explanation.surface: Manchester United once more have done for Arsenal, the Gunners, at the same ground as before.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is also the nickname of Arsenal football club, which gives the surface its match report feel; here it means the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubi supra is a Latin reference phrase meaning where stated above, used in footnotes to point back to an earlier passage.

clue.text: In England, uniform Zulus wear, but not with animated character

indicators.note: in puts the following letters inside the word for the country
'but not' removes the letter that stands for 'with'

blocks.note: Blighty is old soldiers' slang for Britain or England
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Zulu is Z in the NATO alphabet, so two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of what Zulu warriors in England wear, set beside an animated film figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Uniform and Zulu are both NATO alphabet code words, not clothing and a people. Blighty is old army slang for home, from Hindustani.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz Lightyear is the space ranger toy who stars in Pixar's Toy Story films, a computer-animated cartoon hero.

clue.text: Inactive time after 6 PM, not 9

indicators.note: not takes the Roman numeral that follows away from the number before it
after places the first-named piece at the end, behind what comes from the rest of the clue

blocks.note: the number spelt out
nine in Roman numerals
Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone sits idle in the evening, as long as it is after six rather than nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 PM reads as a time of day, but the number and the Prime Minister are separate pieces; Anthony Eden was PM in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedent is a rare word for sitting, seated and so at rest, from Latin sedere, to sit.

clue.text: Professional mostly dodges some Highland game

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a paid player is a professional, not an amateur
dodges are tricks or ruses

explanation.surface: A professional sportsman mostly ducks out of a Highland Games event.
explanation.walkthrough: Highland game looks like the Highland Games sporting contest; it means game birds shot in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Paitricks is the Scots form of partridges, birds shot for sport, and game in the hunting sense.

clue.text: Gang this crooked? Indeed, pinching large Rolls

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so letters are held inside another word
something that rolls over turns upside down, so in a down clue the word runs the other way

blocks.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed
lg is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Does this gang go astray? Yes, and it pinches a big Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: YEA holds LG to give YELGA, read upwards as AGLEY. The definition alludes to Burns: the best laid schemes 'gang aft agley', go often awry.
explanation.definitionFit: Agley is Scots for askew or awry, and Burns used it of plans that go wrong, so crooked is its meaning.

clue.text: Purple adopted by Nancy’s a strip of something flashy

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: Nancy is a French city, so its word for a is une
plum is a shade of purple

explanation.surface: A girl called Nancy takes up purple and turns it into a strip of something showy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name, but it is the city in Lorraine, so its 'a' is French.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplume is to remove the plumes, the showy feathers, so it means stripping off finery.

clue.text: Leading artist, one on church body, picked up book for Mass

indicators.note: picked up means lifted, so in a down clue the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the leader is No 1, written NO I
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Roman numeral one
in cricket the on side is also the leg side
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A leading painter is one of a church committee and picks up a missal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading artist' reads as one phrase but splits into NO I and RA. The whole string NOIRAILEGNAVE is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangeliarion is a liturgical book containing the Gospel passages read at Mass, arranged for the church year.

clue.text: So-called star reader liked tips on Zola’s novel

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters
novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Zola
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who reads the stars enjoyed the highlights of a novel by Émile Zola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zola's novel' suggests a book by the French author, but novel is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Zadkiel was the pen name of the astrologer Richard Morrison, whose almanac read the stars, hence a pseudonymous astrologer.

clue.text: Solvent or sedative everyone’s taken in party

indicators.note: taken in means admitted inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: all means everyone
a do is a party

explanation.surface: At a party everyone has had either a solvent or a sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': ALL has DO taken in, giving AL-DO-L.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldol is an organic compound formed from acetaldehyde, used as a solvent and formerly as a hypnotic drug.

clue.text: Scottish court’s only keeping a track on Irish comedian

blocks.note: Dave Allen was an Irish comedian
taken as written
rly is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A Scottish court keeps only one track for an Irish comic.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after. Dave Allen was an Irish TV comedian known for his barstool monologues.
explanation.definitionFit: Allenarly is a Scots word meaning solely or exclusively, still found in Scots legal drafting.

clue.text: Help mending torn gardening glove — not dear

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters are pulled into a different order
not takes the word for a term of endearment away from the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is a term of endearment, like dear

explanation.surface: Someone needs help to mend a gardening glove that has torn, a cheap one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not dear' looks like cheap, but it removes LOVE from GLOVE, leaving G to join GARDENING in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A darning egg is the smooth egg-shaped tool put inside a sock so that holes can be darned, an aid to mending.

clue.text: Note fuss about criminal record gets soldier dismissed

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround what follows

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
ado is fuss
form is slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: A note of protest about someone's criminal past gets a soldier thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The note and the fuss together go around the record. Form is British slang for a history of convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformado was an officer whose company was disbanded, kept on without a command, a soldier stood down.

clue.text: What rook might go past small headland?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a rook's call is caw

explanation.surface: Where might a rook fly on its way past a little headland?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might go' suggests a chess move or a flight path; it means the sound a rook makes, which follows S.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaw, or skaw, is a promontory in Orkney and Shetland dialect, a point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Scot who’s lent a lot of notes to me?

blocks.note: a wad is a thick roll of banknotes
the speaker of a crossword clue is its setter

explanation.surface: Is this a Scotsman who has lent me a big bundle of cash?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' in a clue is the setter, a common convention. A wadset was a Scots mortgage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law a wadsetter held land as security for money he had advanced, so he was a creditor or mortgagee.

clue.text: Every so often in cases framing neat sentiment

indicators.note: every so often means at regular intervals, so only alternate letters are kept
a frame goes around a picture, so the kept letters surround the next word

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters
neat is an old word for cattle, as is kine

explanation.surface: A tidy feeling turns up from time to time in some legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat here is the noun for cattle, as in neat's-foot oil, not the adjective for tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ickiness is cloying, sugary sweetness of feeling, and sentiment in the sense of mawkish sentimentality.

clue.text: What’s revealed in briefs — and in revolutionary flameproof nightie?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow
something revolutionary turns right round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Underwear gives something away, as does a fireproof nightdress worn by a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: Briefs suggests underwear; here they are briefings, which reveal information.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefing passes on information, and info is the casual short form of that word.

clue.text: Changing hands, judged unfavourably: in other words, “pronounced”

indicators.note: the hands are right and left, so one hand's letter is swapped for the other's

blocks.note: criticised means judged unfavourably

explanation.surface: A property passes to new owners after being judged harshly, pronounced so in other words.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in CRITICISED becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A clitic is a word, like 'm in I'm, that is spoken as part of a neighbouring word, so cliticised means sounded inside another word.

clue.text: One to rope in for cycling no longer free

indicators.note: cycling sends a letter round from the front to the back

blocks.note: to lasso is to rope in
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is lassoed for a bike ride and is no longer at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: LASSO plus I, then the L cycles round to the end. 'No longer' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Assoil is an archaic verb meaning to absolve, acquit or release from guilt, so to set free.

clue.text: Without retreating, ice spar affected water conservation method

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the letters run the other way
affected means altered, so the letters are changed in order

blocks.note: ex is Latin for out of, without
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ice spar, a mineral, has been worked on by some method of saving water.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice spar is a real mineral, which sells the surface; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeriscape gardening uses drought-tolerant plants to cut irrigation, a landscaping method that saves water.

clue.text: 80-per-cent initial reduction in mortgage, perhaps, key figures having supposedly fallen

indicators.note: the first letter, read as a Roman number, is cut by four fifths and replaced by the smaller numeral

blocks.note: a mortgage is one type of loan
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Lenders slash a mortgage by 80 per cent, and the key numbers have dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: L is 50 in Roman numerals; reduce it by 80 per cent and it is 10, X. Key figures reads like statistics, but key gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Xoana are primitive wooden cult statues of ancient Greece, which tradition held had dropped from heaven.

clue.text: Hint of air and sky all see tho’ never outside

indicators.note: never the outside means the edges are dropped and only the centres kept

blocks.note: the centre letter
the centre letter
the centre letter
the centre letter
the centre letter
surface padding, giving the line its poetic tone

explanation.surface: A poetic line about air and sky that everyone can see, though never from outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Five three-letter words each give up their middle letter; tho' just keeps the archaic poetic tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkle is a dialect verb meaning to give an inkling, to suggest or let something be known indirectly.

clue.text: Painter’s materials interspersed with hint of light medium

indicators.note: interspersed means scattered among, so letters are slotted between others
a hint is just a trace, the first letter of the word

blocks.note: kit is equipment, materials
first letter of light
M is the abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: An artist's supplies, with a trace of light medium mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: L and M are each slotted into KIT, one after K and one after I. The 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Klimt was the Austrian artist of The Kiss, a leading figure of the Vienna Secession.

clue.text: Old lady put out when one surrounds clan leaders

indicators.note: surrounds means goes all round, so the later pieces enclose the earlier

blocks.note: as means when
Roman numeral one
one's old lady is one's mother, ma
KO, knock out, puts a boxer out

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is upset when someone encircles the heads of her clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like upset, but it is a knockout. The word, plural of inkosi, is South African, from Xhosa and Zulu.
explanation.definitionFit: Amakosi are chiefs in Xhosa and Zulu society, the traditional heads of tribes and clans.

clue.text: Translator, one who dispenses with alternative end to chapter

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
an alternative is something put in place of another, so one letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: a chemist dispenses medicines
last letter of chapter

explanation.surface: A translator, someone who does without a different ending to a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispenses with' looks like a phrase meaning does without; it is a pharmacist who dispenses, and C is replaced by R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhemists were the Catholic scholars at Rheims who produced the English New Testament of 1582.

clue.text: Patron of poetry’s retired to cut a piece of verse

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, gone back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
to lop is to cut
a line is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: Poetry's patron has stepped back so as to trim a bit of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word also cuts into A LINE, sitting between A and LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apolline means of or like Apollo, the Greek god who presided over poetry and music, so Apollo's.

clue.text: Goddess’s sort of dark coat

blocks.note: -ish means sort of
tar is a dark coating

explanation.surface: A goddess wears a dark coat of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishtar was the Babylonian and Assyrian deity of love, fertility and war.
